item.title: Firefox Open New Tab Next to Current Tab
item.description:
If you have a lot of tabs open, it’s very irritating when you open a new tab with Ctrl + T only to have it be opened at the very end of your tabs. For a long time the way I used to work around this was to duplicate the tab that I was in and then change the URL .

Turns out there is a way to change this default behaviour in Firefox. Open about:config and change broser.tabs.insertAfterCurrent to true. This setting seems to also override browser.tabs.insertRelatedAfterCurrent, so if you have the browser.tabs.insertAfterCurrent set to true, this will also be true irrespective of it’s value.

item.title: Olympic Designs
item.description: I was researching about Otl Aicher who was the lead designer for the 1972 Munich Olympics. It turns out he was one of the designer whose pictograms inspired the DOT pictograms which then went on to inspire the ubiquitous signage pictograms that we see everyday I could find atleast one reference which definitively says that DOT pictograms were used during the standardization process of ISO 7001 in the book “The Politics of Design” by Ruben Pater, in the Chapter Symbols and Icons, subsection Icons of Inequality . I used to think that emoji’s and related pictograms were actually introduced during the Japanese Olympic, but from what I could figure out from my limited research, the genealogy of emoji’s is much more diverse. Nonetheless, Otl Aicher did seem to have consulted with the designer of the 1964 Japanese Olympic Games. As such there is a direct line of inspiration from the Japanese Olympics to the current signage.

item.title: Hello Again!
item.description:
It’s been quite a while!

I redid the blog, this time with my own custom design which I implemented myself What is implementing yourself in this age of LLM’s? For me and for this blog, it was writing the code mostly myself but occassionally referring to LLM’s for help . Apart from the cosmetic changes, stealing a good idea from other blogs, I have also added a new section called Notes, which is where this post is. The idea is that this would allow me to write about and link to things which might be topical or things that I find interesting, but which are not long form articles. Currently I don’t have a hard-and-fast rule on what is an article and what is not, but I think it would be fairly obvious as I get to writing each of them.
